description:
Calculate the elongation velocity of the mitotic spindle during anaphase using the built-in 'Mitosis' sample.

1. Open the sample: File > Open Samples > Mitosis (26MB, 5D stack).
2. Create a Maximum Intensity Projection (Z-Project) to flatten the Z-stack.
3. Split Channels to isolate the spindle (Green/Tubulin) from the DNA (Red).
4. Measure the pole-to-pole distance (center to center of the bright spindle poles) at Frame 30 and Frame 45.
   - Use the Line tool to measure distance in microns (µm).
   - Note: You must find the time interval between frames in Image > Properties to calculate velocity.
5. Calculate the elongation velocity in µm/min.
   Formula: (Distance_F45 - Distance_F30) / (Time_F45 - Time_F30)

6. Save the processed green channel projection image to '~/Fiji_Data/results/spindle/spindle_projection.tif'.
7. Create a text report at '~/Fiji_Data/results/spindle/velocity_report.txt' with the following format:
   Distance_F30: [Value] um
   Distance_F45: [Value] um
   Time_Delta: [Value] min
   Velocity: [Value] um/min
